summary.prose: Three small changes make the graph store's write transactions all-or-nothing: the write helper, then the migration runner and first boot, switch to lmdb's child transaction, and a pin test guards the library behaviour the fix rests on.

tasks.title: withWriteTxn runs its synchronous callback as an lmdb child transaction
tasks.summary: In src/db/graph/store.ts:882-910, withWriteTxn calls `store.root.childTransaction(() => fn(store))` in place of `store.root.transaction(...)` at :886, wrapped in Promise.resolve (a nested child returns a plain value); its callback type no longer allows a Promise result, and a thenable result is refused by throwing 'withWriteTxn callbacks must be synchronous' inside the child (aborting it). The race against the probe timer, confirmLockLoss and recordLocksLost stay as they are. src/db/graph/__tests__/store-health.test.ts: the locks-lost test (:84-107) also counts childTransaction; the slow-healthy-write test (:145-165) uses a synchronous callback with store.root.childTransaction wrapped to resolve after a delay past the bound.
acceptanceChecks: A withWriteTxn callback that writes in two sub-DBs and throws rejects with its own error and leaves nothing, in-process and after a reopen
Of two callers queued together, one throwing and one succeeding, only the successful one's writes are kept
An async callback is refused with 'withWriteTxn callbacks must be synchronous' and keeps nothing; the type rejects it (@ts-expect-error)
store-health.test.ts passes with childTransaction counted and the slow write probed at each bound
All existing db and graph suites pass

tests.name: src/db/graph/__tests__/write-txn-atomic.test.ts: a throwing callback leaves nothing (in-process and after a reopen); a throwing and a succeeding caller queued together; an async callback refused and keeping nothing
src/db/graph/__tests__/store-health.test.ts: no library transaction (childTransaction counted) after locks-lost; the slow healthy write probed at each bound with a synchronous callback

tasks.title: The migration runner and the first-boot write run as child transactions
tasks.summary: src/db/graph/migrations.ts:442-448 runs each step and its version write in `store.root.childTransaction(async () => { ... })` (steps may stay async: they run inside the store's open before any caller can reach the store) and the comment at :444-446 says what holds; the first-boot write at src/db/graph/store.ts:607-610 uses `root.childTransaction`. src/db/graph/__tests__/migrations.test.ts gains row assertions: a step that writes rows and throws leaves neither its rows nor its version write, earlier steps stay committed.
acceptanceChecks: A throwing migration step leaves neither its rows nor its version write; earlier steps stay committed
A fresh store still boots at the current version with the shared-modules rows

tests.name: src/db/graph/__tests__/migrations.test.ts: a throwing step leaves neither its rows nor its version write; earlier steps stay committed

tasks.title: Pin lmdb's transaction behaviour and the store's open options
tasks.summary: New src/db/graph/__tests__/lmdb-txn-semantics.test.ts: in a fresh process after a reopen (the store-child.ts harness or a direct child), root.transaction keeps a throwing callback's write, root.childTransaction and root.transactionSync discard it. A test that the store opens without useWritemap (child transactions available). lock-loss-detection.test.ts and lock-loss-reproduction.test.ts pass unchanged.
acceptanceChecks: The pin test fails if lmdb starts discarding root.transaction writes or keeping childTransaction ones

tests.name: src/db/graph/__tests__/lmdb-txn-semantics.test.ts: in a fresh process after a reopen, root.transaction keeps a throwing callback's write, childTransaction and transactionSync discard it; the store opens without useWritemap

testStrategyCoverage.lldStrategyItem: withWriteTxn: a callback that writes rows in two sub-DBs and throws rejects with its own error and leaves nothing behind (read back in-process and after closeGraphStore/reopen); a callback that returns commits as before (src/db/graph/__tests__/write-txn-atomic.test.ts)
withWriteTxn: two callers queued together, one throwing and one succeeding: only the successful caller's writes are kept

withWriteTxn: a callback that returns a Promise is refused with 'withWriteTxn callbacks must be synchronous' and leaves nothing behind (the type also rejects it at compile time, checked with // @ts-expect-error)
runMigrations: a step that writes rows and throws leaves neither its rows nor the version write; earlier steps stay committed (extends src/db/graph/__tests__/migrations.test.ts with row assertions)
store-health: after locks-lost no library transaction is called, counting childTransaction as well as transaction and transactionSync (src/db/graph/__tests__/store-health.test.ts)
the store opens without useWritemap, so child transactions are available

store-health 'slow healthy write' keeps its intent with a synchronous callback: the test wraps store.root.childTransaction so its promise resolves only after a delay past the bound (a test seam, restored afterwards; no library transaction is held open, which would nest the write instead), and asserts that the probe ran at each bound, returned every time, and the write completed

lmdb behaviour pin, in a fresh process after a reopen: root.transaction keeps a throwing callback's write; root.childTransaction and root.transactionSync discard it (src/db/graph/__tests__/lmdb-txn-semantics.test.ts)
src/db/graph/__tests__/lock-loss-detection.test.ts and lock-loss-reproduction.test.ts pass unchanged (withWriteTxn still reports 'write-timeout-probe' within the bound)
